strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Moves the first post-admission Mode Pack route boundary from caller-supplied typed-target assembly into Rust-owned replay-safe journey continuation.
Continues an admitted journey through existing headless.run.drive/headless.run.advance authority while preserving explicit stop-boundary behavior.
Keeps route eligibility, target derivation, checkpoint binding, replay, and denial in the Rust runtime rather than the VSIX or headless caller.
Binds journey-route resume to source checkpoint fingerprints and bounded post-route progress so a headless caller can recover context from runtime-owned state.
Returns bounded route-resume metadata with source checkpoint fingerprint, result continuation, post-route progress, replay state, and next action.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with supporting agent_loop, runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, context_management, and progress_visualization.
answers.new_capability: headless.run.drive can accept one explicitly authorized journey_route_resume envelope and derive the selected-candidate fetch target from persisted registry-selection checkpoint evidence without caller-supplied modepack_selected_candidate_fetch_target.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M50.1 admits and first-drives a journey, and M49.3 dispatches caller-supplied typed route targets; neither lets the Rust runtime derive the next journey route target from its own checkpoint evidence.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A scheduled caller would still need external glue to inspect route evidence, build trusted typed Mode Pack targets, and manage lost-response replay outside the Rust execution authority.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M50.1 journey admission, M49.3 caller-supplied Mode Pack route dispatch, and R7.1/R7.2 control-plane guard work because it changes post-admission runtime continuation behavior.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing headless.run.drive method is extended with one bounded journey_route_resume envelope and result metadata.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase adds executable route continuation, checkpoint validation, ledger evidence, and replay metadata rather than a report, digest, readiness, history, or inspection surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The Rust runtime validates the journey fingerprint, session sequence, route kind, and source checkpoint fingerprint, derives a ModePackSelectedCandidateFetchTarget from persisted selection evidence, executes the route through existing continuation authority, persists bounded resume evidence, and replays without duplicate route side effects.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A headless controller can continue a Golden Journey from runtime-owned evidence after a crash or boundary stop without reconstructing trusted target identity in the caller.
answers.milestone_progress: Establishes the first runtime-derived post-admission route continuation needed before M50 can reach end-to-end journey completion.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M50.2 updates the current and archived phase-value manifests for a product runtime journey-route-resume phase. Review must confirm the manifest change does not weaken phase-value, product-completion, diagnostics, or source-of-truth enforcement.

exit_criteria: headless.run.drive accepts one authorized bounded journey-route resume envelope without adding a new RPC
the runtime derives a selected-candidate fetch target from persisted registry-selection checkpoint evidence instead of requiring caller-supplied modepack_selected_candidate_fetch_target

journey-route resume validates journey fingerprint, current session sequence, route kind, source checkpoint fingerprint, source selection identity, authorization, and replay identity before route side effects
unsupported route kind, missing authorization, stale checkpoint fingerprint, missing checkpoint, and mixed explicit target requests fail closed without new fetch/drive/resume evidence
replaying the same resume request returns committed bounded metadata without duplicating selected-candidate fetch, drive, or journey-route resume ledger evidence

resume result metadata contains bounded journey/task/run/session/drive handles, route kind, source checkpoint fingerprint, derived target class, result advance/continuation id, post-route progress, next action, replay flag, and deterministic resume fingerprint
VSIX validators accept the bounded route-resume protocol shape and reject malformed fingerprints, false authorization, mixed explicit targets, unsupported route kind, and raw/unbounded fields
no report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, generic scheduler, new RPC, or VSIX-owned policy is added
behavior_evidence: Rust behavior test headless_run_drive_journey_route_resume_derives_fetch_target_and_replays covers authorized runtime-derived selected-candidate fetch target execution without caller-supplied fetch target, stale source checkpoint denial, bounded metadata, replay, and duplicate-free fetch/resume evidence
Rust M50.1 journey admission tests continue covering journey admission denial, malformed journey ids, mixed admission targets, and conflicting replay boundaries

VSIX runtimeClient protocol tests accept valid journey_route_resume params and journey_route_resume result metadata, reject mixed explicit targets, non-unit route budgets, malformed fingerprints, unsupported route kind, and raw route-resume fields

accepted_capability: Runtime-derived headless journey route resume for FetchSelectedModePackCandidateExplicitly through existing headless.run.drive
behavior_evidence: cargo test -p brownie-runtime headless_run_drive_journey_route_resume_derives_fetch_target_and_replays -- --nocapture passes the route-resume derivation, stale denial, replay, and duplicate-free ledger behavior test
pnpm --filter brownie-vsix test -- runtimeClient.test.ts passes protocol validator coverage for bounded journey_route_resume params and results
cargo check --workspace passes with the new Rust protocol/runtime/store types
safety_boundary: reuses existing headless.run.drive and headless.run.advance authority; no new JSON-RPC method is added
only FetchSelectedModePackCandidateExplicitly is supported in this phase
route resume cannot mix journey admission, caller-supplied explicit Mode Pack targets, context budgets, or completion finalization authorization
the source registry-selection checkpoint fingerprint and current session sequence must match before route side effects
RPC and ledger evidence is bounded to ids, enum values, hashes, fingerprints, replay state, and next-action classes
non_goals: no generic workflow engine, scheduler, daemon, or background worker
no additional route families beyond selected-candidate fetch
no automatic apply, recovery, verification retry, provider retry, parent join, shell, git, network, or service expansion
no report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, or capability summary surface
rejected_alternatives: generic route executor for all Mode Pack steps
mixing provenance verification, approval, replacement, or completion closure into the same phase
technical_debt: M50.2 supports exactly one route family; provenance verification, approval, replacement, and closure remain caller-owned until later phases.
The runtime monolith and large behavior-test module remain maintainability risks; module splitting should follow stable behavior slices rather than block Golden Journey capability.

Route resume currently requires the caller to provide the expected source checkpoint fingerprint; a later phase may expose or select that fingerprint through a more ergonomic bounded journey state contract without adding report-only surfaces.
next_capability_rationale: After M50.2 merges, the next distinct M50 phase should derive the next post-fetch route boundary such as provenance verification from bounded fetch evidence or close a completed journey from runtime state.
Do not add another wrapper around route state; keep moving route boundaries from caller-owned target assembly into Rust-owned replay-safe continuation.
